content.comment_body: Since it's an LCD, I expect that keeping the backlight on all the time will eventually cause the screen to fade. I know you can set the backlight to always be on through the menu options, but is it possible to use an FBD program to control the backlight's on/off times? For example, having it on from 9am to 5pm, and otherwise only turning on when a button on the base module is pressed. I noticed various timers and specific markers for the backlight, so I'm curious if this can be done programmatically. Thanks,

Yes, you can have the backlight stay on at certain times using the backlight markers together with a weekly timer. However, in this case, pressing a button won't automatically turn the backlight on anymore.
Additionally, you can manage the backlight via your program using an input and a timer for manual control. [url]
Thanks for the response, I appreciate your help. Not being able to activate the backlight by pressing a button isn't suitable for my needs.
Thank you, I'll consider your suggestion.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for more flexible and automated control over the LCD backlight offered by their hardware. They would like to program its ON/OFF state based on time schedules and button inputs. The default settings allow it to remain always on, but creating more advanced control through programmable logic appears challenging, especially since automatic activation by button press can be lost. Users also worry about screen degradation from permanent backlighting.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to program the LCD backlight to follow a scheduled pattern, but also retain activation by button press. Their goal is to balance screen longevity with convenient usability.
